t: This is the Wallace Collection, a free museum housed in Hertford House on Manchester Square, once the townhouse of the Marquesses of Hertford. It is named for Sir Richard Wallace, who built up the collection with the Hertford family. After his death, his widow Lady Wallace left about 5,500 artworks to the nation, in line with his wishes, and the museum opened here thirteen years after she died. Inside, twenty-five galleries hold French eighteenth-century paintings and furniture, arms and armour, porcelain and Old Master paintings.
